commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
instructions: Grip an overhead bar with both hands, palms facing away, hands just outside shoulder-width.
Step off the support and let your body hang with straight arms, feet off the ground.
Keep your shoulders pulled slightly down away from your ears — don't shrug up.
Breathe calmly and hang for time. Step back onto the support to finish.
longevityNotes: Grip strength is one of the most-studied correlates of healthy aging, and the dead hang builds it alongside shoulder health and spinal decompression. It's also zero-impact and self-limiting — you simply let go when you're done. Accumulate 2-3 minutes of total hang time per week; it doubles as a daily shoulder-health habit.
name: Dead Hang

progression.loadingGuidance: Add 5-10 seconds per set when you can finish all sets without grip failure.
progression.regressTo: Feet-supported hang (toes on a box, partial bodyweight)

safetyNotes: Skip or modify if you have an acute shoulder injury or uncontrolled high blood pressure. Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain rather than muscular fatigue.
